survey: Spiral or tiered topiary: four stacked leafy tiers that get smaller toward a pointed top. It sits upright in a round planter ring made of pale stone blocks, filled with brown soil. The ring stands on a curved path of terracotta paving. Behind it are a lawn, a wooden bench with a flower pot on the left, a small lantern post on the right, and a hedge wall. The camera looks down at roughly 20–25°. The planter ring is an open ellipse showing the soil inside, with the tops of the back blocks visible and the side faces of the front blocks large. The paving tiles and the path's curved curb get smaller and flatter toward the back, consistent with that view. The divisions between the topiary tiers curve downward in the middle, so they are also seen from above. Each tier's leaves get smaller and turn sideways toward its edges, following the rounded surface. The bench seat and the lantern cap are also seen slightly from above. The topiary trunk stands vertically on the soil in the centre of the ring, and the ring rests flat on the paving.
